phases.objective: Classify repository automation and reject branch-specific or unregistered temporary tooling before merge.

e2e_journeys.actor: pull request author or repository automation agent
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Repository Tool Lifecycle Governance pull-request workflow
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A bounded canonical report accepts registered reusable tooling and rejects one-off triggers, branch literals, pull-request writes, force pushes, and self-deleting workflows.
steps: Checkout the exact pull-request head SHA and inventory changed files against the exact base SHA.
Load the machine-readable repository maintenance tool policy.
Classify changed workflows and scripts as registered reusable tools, temporary artifacts, or product runtime.
Write machine-readable and human-readable lifecycle reports before enforcement.
Fail the required check when any governed rule is violated.
assertions: A branch-specific write workflow is rejected.
A pull-request-triggered workflow with contents write is rejected.
Trigger files and versioned one-off patch runners are rejected.
Unregistered scripts under the governed tool root are rejected.
A registered read-only lifecycle guard and compliant manually dispatched workflow are accepted.
The report identifies the exact candidate and base SHA and declares secrets_included=false.

phases.objective: Make the lifecycle rule an automatic pull-request gate and preserve canonical evidence without manual Job-log reconstruction.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A pull request changing repository automation
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The reviewer reads one exact-head lifecycle artifact and the check blocks merge until temporary artifacts are removed or promoted.
steps: Run the guard regression before evaluating the candidate.
Upload the report even when enforcement fails.
Expose the bounded report in the GitHub Step Summary.
Enforce the report result without treating Job logs as status authority.
assertions: The canonical artifact is uploaded on both pass and fail paths.
The PR template requires automation classification and cleanup confirmation.
The documentation defines promotion and deletion rules for future tools.
The guard itself is registered as a permanent read-only repository tool.

phases.objective: Fail closed on candidate policy tampering, unsafe registered tool bodies, undeclared write authority, missing registration, workflow self-modification, and ambiguous tool lifecycle.

e2e_journeys.actor: automation attempting an unsafe repository mutation
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Changed workflow, candidate policy, or registered maintenance script
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Unsafe automation or policy weakening is blocked with a bounded finding code and remediation before it reaches main.
steps: Reject candidate policy changes that disable mandatory rules, remove protected branches, alter the governed root, or invalidate the canonical guard registration.
Retain baseline forbidden one-shot and trigger patterns even when the candidate policy omits them.
Read every registered maintenance tool entrypoint and compare declared mode with detected repository mutation behavior.
Detect pull-request write-all authority and repository pushes independently of the declared GitHub token permission block.
Require mutating tools and workflows to verify expected head identity and reject main and Production.
Detect work-branch literals, force push, and workflow self-deletion.
assertions: No candidate can disable a mandatory safety rule in the same pull request that introduces unsafe automation.
No registered read-only tool can contain git push or API mutation behavior.
No mutating registered tool can omit a changed-path allowlist, expected-head verification, or protected-branch rejection.
No pull-request workflow can gain write authority through permissions write-all.
No external credential or read-scoped workflow can bypass mutation guards when its body performs a repository write.
No temporary automation can pass by hiding inside a versioned or once-suffixed workflow name.
Deleting a prohibited temporary artifact is accepted as remediation rather than reported as surviving automation.
Findings contain no repository secret or changed-file content.

phases.objective: Observe the guard across several unrelated pull requests and tune only documented false positives without weakening the core safety rules.
Make Repository Tool Lifecycle Governance a required main-branch check after successful canary observation.
